title: Triangle areas
goal: I can find the area of a triangle with the height that meets the base at a right angle. I can find areas of shapes made from triangles.

learn.intro: The area of a triangle is 1/2 × base × height. The height meets the base at a right angle. A slanting side is not the height, unless the triangle has a right angle there.

example.problem: Find the area of triangle ABC. The dashed line is the height.
steps: Choose the base: AB = 21 cm. The height meets AB at a right angle: it is 8 cm.
The sides AC = 10 cm and BC = 17 cm are slanting. They are not heights, so we do not use them.
example.answer: The area of triangle ABC is 84 cm².

howto.title: How to
steps: Find a base and the height that meets it at a right angle.
Multiply base × height. Then halve it.

try.text: Triangle PQR has a right angle at Q. PQ = 9 cm, QR = 12 cm and PR = 15 cm. Find its area. {b} cm²
try.explanation: The right angle is at Q, so the sides PQ and QR meet at a right angle. Take QR as the base and PQ as the height. 1/2 × 12 × 9 = 54. The side PR = 15 cm is slanting, so it is not used.

items.text: Find the area of each triangle. The dashed line is the height.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Triangle (a): {b} cm²

parts.label: b
parts.text: Triangle (b): {b} cm²

items.explanation: Use the dashed height with the base it meets at a right angle. (a) 1/2 × 6 × 4 = 12. (b) 1/2 × 16 × 8 = 64. The slanting sides (5 and 5, 10 and 10) are not used.

items.text: Triangle PQR has a right angle at Q.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The area is {b} cm².

parts.label: b
parts.text: With QR as the base, the height is {b} cm.

parts.label: c
parts.text: With PQ as the base, the height is the side   {circ:QR|PR}

items.explanation: (a) 1/2 × 8 × 6 = 24. (b) PQ meets QR at the right angle Q, so the height is PQ = 6 cm. (c) With PQ as the base, the height is QR, because QR meets PQ at a right angle. PR is slanting.

items.text: The area of a triangle is 1/2 × base × height. Find the missing length.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Area 36 cm² and base 9 cm. The height is {b} cm.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Area 45 cm² and height 9 cm. The base is {b} cm.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Area 28 cm² and base 7 cm. The height is {b} cm.

items.explanation: Base × height is 2 times the area. (a) 2 × 36 = 72 and 72 ÷ 9 = 8. (b) 2 × 45 = 90 and 90 ÷ 9 = 10. (c) 2 × 28 = 56 and 56 ÷ 7 = 8.

items.text: ABCD is a rectangle. Point P lies on the top edge DC.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The shaded triangle ABP has area {b} cm².

parts.label: b
parts.text: P slides along DC. The area   {circ:gets greater|gets smaller|stays the same}

items.explanation: (a) The base AB is 12 cm and the height is 7 cm, the distance between the 2 lines. 1/2 × 12 × 7 = 42. (b) Wherever P is on DC, the base is still 12 cm and the height is still 7 cm, so the area stays the same.

items.text: A square has sides of 8 cm. A triangle stands on its top edge, with the same 8 cm as its base. The triangle is 5 cm tall. What is the total area? {b} cm²

figure.alt: a square with a triangle on top

items.explanation: The square is 8 × 8 = 64 cm². The triangle is 1/2 × 8 × 5 = 20 cm². Add: 64 + 20 = 84 cm².

items.text: ABCD is a rectangle. Point E lies on the top edge DC. Triangle ABE is shaded.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The shaded area is {b} cm².

parts.label: b
parts.text: The area that is not shaded is {b} cm².

items.explanation: (a) 1/2 × 14 × 9 = 63. (b) The rectangle is 14 × 9 = 126 cm². 126 - 63 = 63. The 2 white triangles also add to half of the rectangle.

items.text: Each square on the grid is 1 cm². Find the area of the triangle. {b} cm²
items.explanation: The base AB is 6 squares long. The top point C is 5 squares above the base, so the height is 5. 1/2 × 6 × 5 = 15 cm².

items.text: Look at triangle ABC. Its height AH is outside the triangle. Find the area of triangle ABC. {b} cm²
items.explanation: Use BC as the base. The height from A meets the line BC extended at a right angle at H, and it is 15 cm. The base is only BC = 12 cm, not BH. 1/2 × 12 × 15 = 90. The slanting sides 25 and 17 are not used.

items.text: The areas of a square and a triangle are equal. The square has sides of 10 cm. The base of the triangle is 25 cm.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The area of the square is {b} cm².

parts.label: b
parts.text: The height of the triangle is {b} cm.

items.explanation: (a) 10 × 10 = 100. (b) The triangle has area 100 too, so base × height = 200. 200 ÷ 25 = 8. Check: 1/2 × 25 × 8 = 100.

items.text: The shape is a rectangle with a corner cut off. Find its area. {b} cm²
items.explanation: Think of the full rectangle 12 by 9 = 108 cm². The cut-off corner is a right-angled triangle. Its legs are 12 - 8 = 4 cm along the top and 9 - 4 = 5 cm down the right side. Its area is 1/2 × 4 × 5 = 10. The shape is 108 - 10 = 98 cm².

items.text: A triangle has an area of 9 cm². Its base and height are whole numbers of cm.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many different pairs of base and height are possible? {b}

parts.label: b
parts.text: The pair with a base of 3 cm has a height of {b} cm.

items.explanation: Base × height = 18. The pairs are 1 and 18, 2 and 9, 3 and 6, 6 and 3, 9 and 2, 18 and 1: 6 pairs. A base of 3 goes with a height of 6.

items.text: Circle True or False.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The height of a triangle meets its base at a right angle.   {circ:True|False}

parts.label: b
parts.text: Any slanting side of a triangle can be used as the height.   {circ:True|False}

parts.label: c
parts.text: A triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm has the same area as a triangle with base 6 cm and height 10 cm.   {circ:True|False}

items.explanation: (a) True: that is what makes it the height. (b) False: a slanting side does not meet the base at a right angle. (c) True: both have area 1/2 × 10 × 6 = 30 cm².

items.text: Triangle PQR has a right angle at Q. Its sides are 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm. Now use the 10 cm side PR as the base. The height from Q to PR is {b} cm.
items.hint: Find the area first. Then use the 10 cm side as the base.
items.explanation: The area does not depend on which side is the base. Use the 2 sides at the right angle: 1/2 × 8 × 6 = 24 cm². Now the base is 10 cm: 1/2 × 10 × height = 24, so 5 × height = 24 and the height is 4.8 cm.

items.text: ABCD is a rectangle, 14 cm by 10 cm. M is the middle of BC. N is the middle of CD. How much area does the shaded triangle AMN cover? {b} cm²

figure.alt: rectangle ABCD with the shaded triangle AMN

items.hint: Take the 3 white triangles away from the rectangle.
items.explanation: The rectangle is 14 × 10 = 140 cm². White triangle ABM: 1/2 × 14 × 5 = 35. White triangle MCN: legs 5 and 7, 1/2 × 5 × 7 = 17.5. White triangle ADN: 1/2 × 10 × 7 = 35. White total: 35 + 17.5 + 35 = 87.5. Shaded: 140 - 87.5 = 52.5 cm².

items.text: The area of triangle ABC is 72 cm². D is on BC and BD is 1/3 of BC. E is the middle of AD.

figure.alt: triangle ABC with D on BC

parts.label: a
parts.text: The area of triangle ABD is {b} cm².

parts.label: b
parts.text: The area of triangle BDE is {b} cm².

items.hint: ABD and ABC have the same height. Compare their bases.
items.explanation: (a) Triangles ABD and ABC have the same height from A. The base BD is 1/3 of BC, so ABD is 1/3 of 72 = 24 cm². (b) Triangles BDE and ABD have the same height from B to the line AD. The base DE is half of DA, so BDE is half of 24 = 12 cm².

items.text: ABCD is a square with sides of 16 cm. E lies on AB, 4 cm from A. F is the middle of BC. What is the area of triangle DEF? {b} cm²
items.hint: Take away the 3 white right-angled triangles.
items.explanation: The square is 16 × 16 = 256 cm². White triangle ADE: 1/2 × 16 × 4 = 32. White triangle EBF: EB = 12 and BF = 8, so 1/2 × 12 × 8 = 48. White triangle FCD: 1/2 × 16 × 8 = 64. White total: 32 + 48 + 64 = 144. Shaded: 256 - 144 = 112 cm².

items.text: Each square on the grid is 1 cm². The corners of the triangle are on grid points. Find its area. {b} cm²

figure.alt: tilted triangle on a square grid

items.hint: Draw a rectangle round the triangle. Take away 3 triangles.
items.explanation: The rectangle round the triangle goes from 1 to 7 across and 1 to 6 up: 6 × 5 = 30 cm². Three right-angled triangles are outside the shape: 1/2 × 6 × 2 = 6, 1/2 × 4 × 3 = 6 and 1/2 × 2 × 5 = 5. Together 17. The triangle is 30 - 17 = 13 cm².

items.text:
Beyond Level 5: Corner triangles
Triangle ABC has an area of 96 cm². D is on AB with AD = 1/4 of AB. E is on AC with AE = 1/3 of AC. Find the area of triangle ADE. {b} cm²

figure.alt: triangle ABC with a small triangle ADE

items.hint: Join D to C. Compare ADC with ABC first.
items.explanation: Join D to C. Triangles ADC and ABC have the same height from C, and AD is 1/4 of AB, so ADC = 1/4 of 96 = 24 cm². Now triangles ADE and ADC have the same height from D, and AE is 1/3 of AC, so ADE = 1/3 of 24 = 8 cm². The small triangle is 1/4 × 1/3 = 1/12 of the whole.

items.text: Find the area of the triangle. {b} cm²
items.explanation: The base is 28 cm and the height that meets it at a right angle is 15 cm. 1/2 × 28 × 15 = 210. The slanting sides (17 and 25) are not used.

items.text: A triangle has an area of 54 cm². Its base is 12 cm. Find its height. {b} cm
Find the area of the whole shape. {b} cm²

figure.alt: rectangle with a triangle on its right side

items.explanation: The rectangle is 10 × 6 = 60 cm². The triangle on the right has a base of 6 cm (the side BC) and a height of 4 cm. 1/2 × 6 × 4 = 12. Total: 60 + 12 = 72 cm².

items.text: A garden is a triangle with a base of 18 m and a height of 10 m. One bag of seed covers 6 m². How many bags are needed to cover the whole garden? {b}
items.explanation: The area is 1/2 × 18 × 10 = 90 m². 90 ÷ 6 = 15 bags.
